📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Body recomposition is the fitness goal these days. If you’ve been hearing the term everywhere like I have, and thinking body recompo-what, you’re not alone.

In a recent development, so, what is body recomp? Whether you knew it or not, chances are, you’ve probably pursued it at some point. If you’ve ever set out to reduce body fat or build muscle, you’ve been working toward a body recomposition goal. When people say body recomp these days, they really mean simultaneously losing fat and building muscle, not just one or the other.

Meet the expert: Brittany Busse, MD, is the chief medical officer and cofounder of ViTel Health.

Industry observers note that unlike simply losing weight, this approach isn’t about the number on the scale; it’s about improving the ratio of fat to muscle in your body for better health, performance, and aesthetics. (Oftentimes, when people talk about wanting to look "toned," they're really talking about body recomp, since you need low amounts of body fat to see the muscle you've built up.).

According to recent reports, and, while body recomposition is completely possible, it can be a little more technical than other fitness goals. Here are the core things you need to know to get started on your body recomp journey.

Get started with our exclusive body recomp guide.

According to recent reports, first: a quick refresher. Body composition refers to a percentage breakdown of how much body fat, lean mass (that is, muscle!), and bone you've got on your body. Body recomposition is the process through which you change that breakdown.

These are the five most crucial things to keep in mind when trying to make that happen.

In a recent development, at the most basic level, losing fat requires a calorie deficit; you need to burn more than you consume. Working with a nutritionist or doctor, you can determine exactly what this means for you, but for body recomposition, it's only a slight deficit that you should be shooting for. We’re talking 250 to 500 calories max.

In a recent development, keep in mind: “Weight loss should not be confused with fat loss,” Brittany Busse, MD, the chief medical officer and cofounder of ViTel Health previously told Women's Health. “Much of weight loss can also be loss of muscle mass.”.

And, you don't want to lose muscle mass, particularly if your goal is body recomp. That’s why protein is critical, Dr. Busse states—but it’s just one piece of the puzzle. Tracking all three macros (protein, carbs, and fat) can go a long way in helping you stay full, energized, and strong while pursuing body recomp.

GET MORE INFO ABOUT COUNTING MACROS FOR BODY RECOMP WITH THE WH+ PDF.

Lifting is nonnegotiable. “People should weight train at least three times a week,” Dr. Busse said. “Weight training will build muscle mass, which will inevitably lead to improved metabolic health and fat loss.”.

Keep up your cardio, too. But, if you’re a HIIT addict, you may want to try slowing things down. “Zone 2 cardio is the most effective way to burn fat while sparing muscle. This is exercising at a level where you can hold a ‘breathy’ conversation comfortably for 45-60 minutes,” Dr. Busse said. “Walking on an incline, cycling, and rucking are all examples of Zone 2 workouts,” she said.

It's hard to come up with a training strategy all on your own, so relying on the expertise of trainers to create a program can help make sure you're working your muscles efficiently and effectively.

Women's Health+ has many body recomp-focused programs for people of all experience levels: the 4-Week Walking Plan, the 4-Week Strength Training Plan, the 4-Week Build & Burn Series (which allows you to follow along with dumbbell, barbell, or kettlebell-based workouts), and the Body Recomp Guide.

Recent findings suggest that age, hormones, and genetics all play a role in body composition, as does access to high-quality food and medical care. Not everyone has the same amount of time to spend exercising. So, take it easy on yourself, and if you can, get help and support as you work toward your goals.

Gamers managed to get multiplayer working on GTA 6 for PC before Rockstar Games managed to release GTA 6 for PC. And they're apparently making the console version run better than the original, too.

It has been revealed that A developer going by TeK shared footage Thursday showing multiple players interacting within the same game world in an unofficial PC build of Grand Theft Auto 6. The implementation reportedly supports character and vehicle synchronization, as well as proximity voice chat, running at between 25 and 30 frames per second (FPS).

GTA VI Working Multiplayer, Character, Vehicles & Proximity voice chat. (25-30FPS)#GTAVI #GTA6 pic.twitter.com/PyWvg764zZ.

— TeK (@TeKGameR950) November 26, 2026.

The development comes just a day after Decrypt reported that some AI-assisted ports were struggling to achieve 20 FPS while consuming upwards of 40 GB of system memory.

Recent findings suggest that another development team, known as BoYoo, demonstrated gameplay averaging 27 FPS during a boat mission, using an AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D processor, an Nvidia RTX 5070 Ti graphics card, and 32 GB of RAM. Memory consumption dropped to approximately 15.4 GB, although performance in the more demanding downtown areas of Vice City remains untested.

No son 60 FPS en el GTA de los Mares del SUR en PS5 pero NADA MAL CHAVALES!! pic.twitter.com/L63ALb7JAu.

— NanospeedGamer (@NanospeedGamer) November 26, 2026.

Developers have also demonstrated in-game modification menus, allowing them to manipulate elements of the game for debugging purposes.

Meanwhile, console modders have released a patch that removes GTA 6's 30 FPS cap on jailbroken PS5 and PS5 Pro consoles. The latter reportedly exceeds 50 FPS during gameplay without relying on AI-generated intermediate frames.

It has been revealed that the patch doesn't guarantee a consistent 60 FPS, but it does offer the potential for smoother gameplay and more responsive controls than Rockstar's officially supported version. For some players, modifying their console could arguably provide a better gameplay experience.

The advancements come despite Rockstar's parent company, Take-Two Interactive, successfully taking down 3,007 GitHub repositories associated with Project Leonida, one of the most prominent efforts to bring the game to PC using AI coding tools.

Developers are using AI to reverse-engineer a leaked Xbox build of the game and adapt its code to run on computers, dramatically accelerating a process that traditionally required extensive manual work.

Rockstar has historically made PC gamers wait. Grand Theft Auto 5 arrived on PC in April 2015, roughly 19 months after its original console release, while Red Dead Redemption 2 took just over a year.

Generative AI could make that business strategy considerably riskier.

Obbe Vermeij, a former technical director at Rockstar North, warned about precisely this scenario before GTA 6's release.

“I think I would be concerned, if I was Rockstar, that somebody would just take the PS5 version and get AI to change it to PC,” Vermeij told Rock Paper Shotgun in an interview.

Sources indicate that vermeij estimated that such an undertaking could cost tens of thousands of dollars in AI processing. Even if the resulting product fell short of Rockstar's official version, he suggested it could be good enough to satisfy some PC gamers, giving the company an incentive to bring its release dates closer together.

Wall Street has been paying attention, too.

During Take-Two's November 9 earnings call, Raymond James analyst Andrew Marok asked management how AI-assisted reverse engineering and decompilation were affecting the organization's approach to security and development.

Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick acknowledged that piracy would become more challenging, although he maintained that replicating the intended experience of its games would remain technically difficult.

“I think it will be manageable, and we are focused on it,” Zelnick noted.

According to recent reports, there is some academic research suggesting that early piracy can substantially affect video game sales. A 2024 study published in Entertainment Computing by researcher William Volckmann examined games protected by Denuvo, an anti-piracy technology, and estimated average revenue losses of 20% when that protection was broken particularly early in a game's commercial life.

That figure cannot be directly extrapolated to GTA 6, which has yet to enter the PC market. But a sufficiently polished unofficial port distributed for free months before Rockstar's commercial release could reduce the number of players willing to pay full price for the same story they have already completed.

Sources indicate that rockstar would still have advantages, including official multiplayer servers, technical support, downloadable content, and a more polished gaming experience. The unofficial multiplayer implementation remains far removed from the scale of GTA Online, and none of the community projects has independently demonstrated that the entire campaign can be completed reliably.

GTA 6 generated an estimated $3.79 billion in retail sales on its first day alone, according to a regulatory filing by Take-Two. Twenty percent of that would amount to roughly $758 million in lost sales revenue.

Rockstar still hasn't announced a PC release date.

A Handful of Pistachios May Help You Sleep Better, Review Claims

📅 19 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1073 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Could a handful of pistachios before you go to bed really help you sleep better?
  • A review of studies published in Nutrition Research Reviews examines how the nutrients and plant compounds in pistachios might influence sleep health.
  • Pistachios contain several nutrients linked to sleep-related processes, prompting an investigation into whether they might offer benefits beyond their nutritional value.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Could a handful of pistachios before you go to bed really help you sleep better?

A review of studies published in Nutrition Research Reviews examines how the nutrients and plant compounds in pistachios might influence sleep health.

Pistachios contain several nutrients linked to sleep-related processes, prompting an investigation into whether they might offer benefits beyond their nutritional value.

While the findings suggest that pistachios may support sleep, the evidence is inconclusive and warrants further study.

“Pistachios are compelling for sleep research because they bring together several nutrients and plant compounds connected to sleep physiology within one whole food,” noted study author Marie-Pierre St-Onge, PhD, professor of nutritional medicine and director of the Center of Excellence for Sleep & Circadian Research in the Department of Medicine at Columbia University Institute of Nutrition, in a news release.

“Rather than focusing on a single ‘sleep nutrient,’ this review provides a rationale for studying how the complete pistachio food matrix may affect sleep-related pathways,” she continued.

The narrative review examined existing research on pistachios and sleep-related biology.

The researchers explored whether the combination of nutrients in pistachios could promote quality sleep.

Rather than identifying pistachios as a sleep remedy, the researchers outlined biological pathways through which their nutrients and bioactive compounds might influence sleep.

“We were particularly interested in pistachios because they are particularly high in phytomelatonin, polyphenols, and carotenoids, which we noted were plant-derived components that had been shown to have sleep benefits in preclinical studies,” St-Onge told Healthline.

“We also noted their high content of tryptophan and vitamin B6, which are relevant to melatonin production in humans,” she continued.

Pistachios contain several nutrients associated with sleep, including melatonin, which helps regulate the sleep-wake cycle.

Other studies examining the effects of some of these nutrients on sleep offer further context.

A 2021 systematic review and meta-analysis of tryptophan supplementation found that it may reduce wakefulness after sleep onset, particularly at doses of at least 1 gram (g) daily. However, an ounce of pistachios supplies only about 71 mg, which is much less than the doses examined by the researchers.

Additionally, a 2023 review of dietary polyphenols led by St-Onge identified potential links between plant compounds and sleep outcomes, although results varied across studies.

Neither review established that polyphenols or tryptophan from pistachios specifically affected sleep quality.

“I was not surprised that pistachios may help support sleep, given their combination of nutrients involved in sleep regulation,” stated Michelle Routhenstein, MS, a preventive cardiology dietitian at EntirelyNourished, who wasn’t involved in the study.

“Pistachios provide tryptophan, an amino acid the body uses to produce serotonin and melatonin; vitamin B6, which supports these pathways; and magnesium, which plays a role in nervous system function and sleep regulation,” she told Healthline.

The upcoming review highlights the concept of the “food matrix,” or how nutrients and bioactive compounds interact within a whole food.

Instead of investigating tryptophan, magnesium, or melatonin individually, researchers were curious about the combined effects of consuming them together in pistachios.

Laboratory and simulated-digestion research offers clues about how fiber and plant compounds in pistachios and peanuts interact with gut microbes. However, these findings do not establish that eating pistachios changes sleep quality in real-world conditions.

Broader nutrition research also points to a relationship between diet and sleep.

A 2021 review in the Annual Review of Nutrition examined evidence linking dietary patterns and individual nutrients to sleep outcomes. The findings suggest a relationship between sleep and diet, but note that more research is needed to determine cause and effect.

In a nutshell, the current evidence builds a compelling case for pistachios as a sleep aid.

However, it’s too soon to recommend pistachios as a sleep remedy, as many factors may affect sleep quality and insomnia.

“Sleep difficulties can have different underlying causes,” Routhenstein noted. “If inadequate intake of these nutrients is a contributing factor, pistachios may help, but they may not address sleep issues related to other nutrient deficiencies or other causes.”.

Much of the supporting evidence cited in the review comes from studies of individual nutrients, other foods, laboratory experiments, or biological mechanisms rather than from trials involving whole pistachios.

Researchers have also reported significant variations in the melatonin content of pistachios, making the amount in a typical serving difficult to pinpoint.

It has been revealed that additionally, the review received support from American Pistachio Growers, and the corresponding author, St-Onge, serves on its advisory board. Larger studies and clinical trials are needed, ideally without industry funding, to ensure well-rounded results.

Indeed, the authors call for randomized controlled trials examining whether eating pistachios affects sleep outcomes, including sleep quality, duration, and melatonin levels.

“This was a review; we noted that the complete profile of pistachios would make them well-suited to support healthful sleep, but research is needed to evaluate this,” St-Onge told Healthline.

“This is the next step, and something we are actively working on. We also need to better understand what dosage and frequency of consumption would be optimal.”.

Regardless, a handful of pistachios is still considered a healthy choice as part of a balanced diet.

According to recent reports, “A small handful, about 1 ounce of shelled pistachios, is an appropriate portion,” Routhenstein mentioned. “Enjoy them during the day or as a light afternoon or evening snack when you’re hungry.”.

If nutrients like tryptophan help promote sleep, it’s possible that other nuts could yield similar results.

“Other nuts, such as almonds and walnuts, may offer similar benefits because they also contain nutrients involved in sleep regulation,” Routhenstein said.

“Early research is encouraging, but it’s too soon to say how much they might help.”.

Other foods, like turkey, also contain tryptophan.

Industry observers note that “For someone allergic to nuts, foods such as tofu, beans, oats, eggs, dairy, and fish can provide tryptophan, which the body uses to make serotonin and melatonin,” Routhenstein said. “The goal is to meet their nutrient needs rather than rely on one food to improve sleep.”.

Sleep health depends on multiple factors. As such, Routhenstein recommends a personalized approach to getting better sleep, from what you eat and when you eat to addressing any nutritional gaps.

Recent findings suggest that “I would also encourage regular, balanced meals throughout the day to support blood sugar management, especially for those with diabetes, while avoiding large meals close to bedtime,” Routhenstein mentioned. “Caffeine later in the day and alcohol in the evening are also worth considering as possible sleep disruptors.”.

According to recent reports, volkswagen revealed how much its new ID. Cross will cost, with prices starting at around $35,000 in the UK. But if you’re hoping to get the cheaper version, you’ll have to wait a bit longer.

After opening orders for the ID. Cross in Europe in July, Volkswagen is preparing to launch the entry-level electric SUV in the UK.

Industry observers note that the ID. Cross is the all-electric equivalent of the T-Cross, Volkswagen’s smallest and most affordable SUV in Europe and the UK.

Following the ID. Polo, the ID. Cross is the latest from Volkswagen’s electric urban family of compact cars.

It has been revealed that the electric SUV is 4,153 mm long, about the same length as the T-Cross, but its dedicated MEB+ platform offers more interior space. It seats five and offers a 475-liter boot, 20 liters more than the gas-powered T-Cross with the rear seats pushed all the way forward.

Industry observers note that when the rear seats are folded, the electric ID. Cross offers up to 1,345 liters of overall luggage volume.

Like in Europe, the Volkswagen ID. Cross will be available with two battery packs in the UK: a 37 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) pack and a 52 kWh nickel-manganese-cobalt (NMC) pack.

According to recent reports, the ID. Cross with the larger 52 kWh battery offers up to 265 miles of WLTP range, while the 37 kWh version provides up to 194 miles of WLTP range.

With DC fast charging of up to 105 and 88 kW, Volkswagen mentioned the vehicle’s battery can charge from 10% to 80% in as little as 23 minutes.

All versions are equipped with vehicle-to-load (V2L) capabilities, allowing it to be used as a mobile power bank for an e-bike, campsite, or other external electronic devices.

Recent findings suggest that inside, the ID. Cross adopts VW’s revamped interior digital cockpit design. Cross adopts VW’s revamped interior digital cockpit design. The setup includes a 10.25″ Digital Cockpit Pro instrument display and a 12.9″ infotainment screen. Based on driver feedback, Volkswagen brought back physical buttons for climate control and other vehicle functions.

Industry observers note that volkswagen will open orders for the ID. Cross Life and Style trims in the UK with the 52 kWh battery and 208 hp (211 PS) motor will go on sale on Thursday, November 19, starting at £30,260 ($40,000) and £33,675 ($44,500), respectively.

Sources indicate that the base ID. Cross Life and Style trims with the 37 kWh battery will go on sale in January 2027, with prices starting at £26,985 ($35,500) and £30,400 ($40,100).

It has been revealed that volkswagen said the 52 kWh version is eligible for the UK government’s £1,500 ($2,000) electric car grant. Eligibility for the 37 kWh versions is expected to be confirmed soon.

In Europe, Volkswagen opened orders for the entry-level ID. Cross Trend last month, starting at €27,995 ($31,000) in Germany, including VAT.

Sources indicate that as the electric counterpart to its popular T-Cross, Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer said the ID. Cross is “modern, reliable, and above all, affordable.”.

Sadly, VW has no plans to bring the ID. Cross to the US. In early 2027, it will launch the upcoming ID. Tiguan, which will replace the outgoing ID.4 SUV.

Industry News: ACOG Strongly Recommends Hormone Therapy for Menopause Symptoms

📅 20 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (927 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) published updated recommendations for menopause management in Obstetrics & Gynecology on October 15.
  • According to recent reports, these expanded recommendations are the most comprehensive guidance to date.
  • According to the ACOG guidance, 50%–92% of females experiencing menopause report VMS.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) published updated recommendations for menopause management in Obstetrics & Gynecology on October 15.

According to recent reports, these expanded recommendations are the most comprehensive guidance to date. They include newly introduced clinical guidelines for menopause hormone therapy (MHT), nonhormonal medications, and nonpharmacological treatment of vasomotor symptoms (VMS), which include hot flashes and night sweats, and sleep and mood changes.

According to the ACOG guidance, 50%–92% of females experiencing menopause report VMS.

Around 16%–66% of females in the United States report menopause-related sleep challenges, and more than one-third of perimenopausal and postmenopausal females report experiencing depressive symptoms.

“In recent years, misconceptions about the risks of hormone therapy have been widespread, which has made some clinicians reluctant to prescribe it and some patients hesitant to use it,” Bruce Pier, MD, clinical professor and associate fellowship director at the University of North Carolina and collaborator on the ACOG clinical practice guidelines, told Healthline.

In a recent development, “This guidance offers a comprehensive review of the evidence to support individualized counseling and shared decision making. Our hope is that it clears up those misconceptions and expands access to treatment.”.

The ACOG is also developing companion guidance for genitourinary syndrome of menopause, expected in 2027.

The ACOG strongly recommends the use of MHT with estrogen and progestogens (or estrogen alone for people without a uterus) for both VMS and vasomotor-related sleep disturbance, in individuals who can use hormones.

It also conditionally recommends conjugated estrogen plus bazedoxifene (Duavee) as an alternative for these issues.

It has been revealed that according to a meta-analysis from 2021 that was cited by the guidelines, estrogen therapy, with or without progestogens, significantly reduced VMS frequency and severity compared to a placebo or no treatment. A 2017 meta-analysis ranked transdermal estradiol plus a progestogen as the most effective option for reducing VMS frequency.

Recent findings suggest that A 2022 systematic review and meta-analysis, also cited by the guidelines, found that MHT was associated with improved self-reported sleep quality. Once again, transdermal therapies revealed some of the largest effects.

The ACOG recommends initiating MHT before age 60 or within 10 years of the onset of natural menopause..

Recent findings suggest that it also suggests that the decision to start MHT for VMS and vasomotor-related sleep disturbances should be based on a shared decision making discussion about an individual’s symptoms and the benefits and risks of therapy. Consideration should also be taken regarding an individual’s:.

Research demonstrates that factors such as race, culture, socioeconomic status, gender identity, and sexual orientation can influence how individuals experience menopause and the care they receive.

According to the SWAN study, Black women reported more menopause symptoms than white women but were less likely to be treated for them.

“This updated document shines a light on these inequities. Clinicians can proactively help right now by asking every patient in midlife about symptoms, rather than waiting for them to bring it up. Long term, we hope this document drives more research funding to understand these gaps and begin closing them,” remarked Pier.

The ACOG stated in the guidelines that, “The available evidence is insufficient to recommend for or against the use of estrogen–progestogen or estrogen-only MHT for the treatment of menopause-related depressive symptoms.”.

It recommends that perimenopausal and postmenopausal individuals who meet the diagnostic criteria for major depressive disorder (MDD) or those whose most noticeable symptom is depression should be treated according to depression management guidelines.

Current treatment guidelines for depression include therapy, medication, or a combination of the two.

Psychological treatments for depression include psychotherapy, such as cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), while antidepressants are among the most commonly prescribed medications.

The ACOG strongly recommends the use of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs) for the management of menopausal symptoms like VMS and depression in individuals who don’t want to use MHT or can’t use it.

At the moment, paroxetine is the only antidepressant that is approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the management of VMS.

The ACOG also strongly recommends the use of neurokinin receptor antagonists to manage VMS and vasomotor-related sleep disturbances in people who don’t desire hormone therapy or can’t use it.

It has been revealed that there are at the moment two neurokinin receptor antagonists approved by the FDA to manage menopause symptoms. Fezolinetant (Veozah) was approved in 2023 to help manage hot flashes. In 2025, the FDA approved elinzanetant (LYNKUET) for the management of moderate to severe VMS due to menopause.

Another nonhormonal treatment for VMS that the ACOG conditionally recommends is gabapentin.

Sources indicate that there are various nonpharmacologic treatments that the ACOG conditionally recommends for the management of VMS, vasomotor-related sleep disturbances, and mood changes. These are treatments that don’t involve the use of medications.

The nonpharmacologic treatments conditionally recommended include:.

It is generally recommended that these interventions are used alongside hormonal or nonhormonal medications.

The ACOG noted that there is not enough evidence to support the efficacy or safety of phytoestrogens, such as soy isoflavones, or herbal supplements, which are not regulated by the FDA in the same way medications are for safety, purity, or efficacy.

According to recent reports, “Menopause is finally getting the attention it deserves, and this document reveals what evidence-based care should look like in this space. It lays out a range of safe, effective options for managing menopause symptoms. My message to anyone struggling with these symptoms is simple: talk to your clinician. You don’t have to suffer through them,” remarked Pier.

Tesla on Autopilot/FSD hit an overturned truck at 71 mph, killing 3

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1499 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Tesla Model 3 drove into an overturned box truck on I-75 near Naples, Florida, killing two of its passengers and a man who had stopped to help.
  • Police and local media covered the May 31 crash as a truck wreck in the dark, and none of it mentioned a driver-assist system.
  • on Sunday, May 31, 2026, the 31-year-old driver of a 2014 Freightliner lost the road near the Pine Ridge Road exit in Collier County, steered back onto southbound I-75, and flipped it, according to the Florida Highway Patrol.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Tesla Model 3 drove into an overturned box truck on I-75 near Naples, Florida, killing two of its passengers and a man who had stopped to help. Tesla’s own report to federal regulators claims Autopilot or “Full Self-Driving” was engaged, at 71 mph.

Police and local media covered the May 31 crash as a truck wreck in the dark, and none of it mentioned a driver-assist system. It’s the latest case in our ongoing investigation into fatal crashes hidden in Tesla’s NHTSA data, and it lands as Tesla’s monthly crash count hits another record.

Just before 4 a.m. on Sunday, May 31, 2026, the 31-year-old driver of a 2014 Freightliner lost the road near the Pine Ridge Road exit in Collier County, steered back onto southbound I-75, and flipped it, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The overturned truck ended up blocking the center and outside lanes.

In a recent development, jonathan Garcia Arias, a 25-year-old Naples man and former Marine, was driving by in a BMW. He pulled over and got out to help the truck driver.

Then a southbound 2023 Tesla with five young men from Naples inside came up on the scene. FHP’s report claims the front of the Tesla hit the underside of the overturned truck and Garcia Arias. Two of the Tesla’s passengers, aged 18 and 19, died at the scene, and Garcia Arias died later in the hospital. The 20-year-old driver and two more passengers were seriously hurt.

It has been revealed that A few days later, FHP used the crash as a warning about stopping near wrecks on the interstate. Senior Trooper Kenn Watson remarked the Tesla driver would have seen only the truck’s underside, with “no lights, no reflectors, nothing warning them.”.

Sources indicate that so that’s the official story. A dark obstacle, a driver who couldn’t see it in time. Nobody remarked a word about Autopilot.

Under NHTSA’s Standing General Order, automakers have to report crashes where a Level 2 driver-assist system was engaged within 30 seconds of impact and someone was killed or hurt. Tesla filed one for this crash.

It identifies the car as a 2023 Model 3 on a highway, flags a traffic incident on the roadway, and marks the automation “Engagement Status” as “Verified Engaged.” That means Tesla confirmed through its own telematics that Autopilot or FSD was on. It logs a pre-crash speed of 71 mph and a fatality, lists the Florida Highway Patrol as the investigating agency, and notes it learned of the crash from police and the media.

Then it blacks out the crash narrative, the software version, and whether the road was within the system’s approved operating domain, all as “confidential business information.” That’s the same redaction Tesla applies to 99.9% of its reports.

Sources indicate that the report also surfaced late. Tesla filed it as a 5-Day report, the urgent category for fatal crashes, but it didn’t land until Tesla’s September filings, more than three months after the crash. And Tesla lists law enforcement as one of the ways it found out about it.

Recent findings suggest that how we matched it: Tesla logged the incident time as 07:56 UTC, which converts to 3:56 a.m. in Florida, two minutes off the 3:54 a.m. in FHP’s report. The city, the highway, the 2023 model year, the month and the fatal outcome all line up, and it’s the only fatal Tesla driver-assist report in Naples that month. It’s the same crash.

It has been revealed that A Tesla on driver-assist going highway speed into the underside of a massive truck, in the dark, in Florida. If that sounds familiar, it should.

According to recent reports, in 2016, Joshua Brown was killed near Williston when his Model S on Autopilot drove under a tractor-trailer crossing the highway. In 2019, Jeremy Banner died in Delray Beach when his Model 3 on Autopilot went under a trailer at 68 mph and had its roof sheared off. In both crashes, neither the driver nor the system braked.

Trooper Watson’s point was that a human couldn’t see the truck. But a big, unlit obstacle sitting across two lanes at night is exactly the kind of thing a driver-assist system is supposed to catch, and Tesla now sells FSD as nearly ready to drive with nobody watching. And an attentive driver could clearly see it, as the BMW driver did, and stop before the Tesla arrived.

We want to be fair about what the data doesn’t prove. “Engaged within 30 seconds” is the reporting trigger. Tesla’s 71 mph may be a telematics snapshot rather than the impact speed. And with the software version redacted, we can’t say whether this was Autopilot or FSD.

The NHTSA release that surfaced this crash, covering filings through October 15, also set a new monthly high. Tesla reported 264 driver-assist crashes in September 2026, beating July’s 236, which was itself a record. That’s up from 135 in March.

In a recent development, september may still grow as late reports come in. This Naples crash shows how late they can be.

It has been revealed that our merged dataset now holds 4,669 Tesla driver-assist crash reports since 2019, 69 of them flagged fatal. The same release added two other fatal reports, both “Verified Engaged” and both covered locally with no mention of driver-assist: a Model Y that hit a tree and burned in El Dorado Hills, California, killing three, and a Model X that hit a signal pole in Naples on September 30, killing a passenger. We’ll lay those out separately.

Sources indicate that three people died on I-75, including a man who got out of his car to help a stranger. Tesla knows its driver-assist was on, knows the speed, holds the telematics, and filed a federal report saying so. Then it sealed everything that would explain what the car did, and the public got a story about a dark truck.

It has been revealed that that's what happens when the system has to identify all objects in the camera frame before it can start to estimate the objects position and then relative distance and then relative velocity. Unrecognizable objects will destroy all your logic. This is a design failure and not something Tesla can actually fix.

According to recent reports, compare that to radars and lidars that directly measure distances and relative velocities of everything in front of the car, regardless of what it is. That is a far better approach because you do not want the car the impact objects on its trajectory regardless of what those objects turn out to be.

Tesla’s whole pitch for FSD is that the car sees better than you do, and yet, Tesla vehicles on Autopilot and FSD keep crashing on stationary objects on the highway. It’s the same failure that killed Joshua Brown and Jeremy Banner years ago. If the system saw the truck and the driver overrode it, Tesla should say so. It was quick to do that in the Katy crash when the data helped it. If the system didn’t see it, that’s a safety defect regulators and owners need to know about.

Sources indicate that either way, the redaction protects Tesla, not the people on the road. It’s the same pattern we found in Vineland and in July’s four fatal crashes, and the crash count keeps setting records.

We’re asking the Florida Highway Patrol for the full crash report, whether its investigators got Tesla’s raw vehicle data, and whether they even knew the system was engaged. If they didn’t, the only party that knows what this car did is the one that sealed the file.

📅 20 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1005 w)

Christina Applegate ‘Not Happy at All’ After Learning She Was Misdiagnosed With MS

📅 20 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1005 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Christina Applegate shared an unexpected health patch on her return to the MeSsy podcast with co-host Jamie-Lynn Sigler.
  • The two actors have detailed their experiences with multiple sclerosis (MS), a neurological disorder that can lead to debilitating symptoms affecting daily functioning and quality of life.
  • Applegate, 54, has been raising awareness about the condition since her initial diagnosis in 2021.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Christina Applegate shared an unexpected health patch on her return to the MeSsy podcast with co-host Jamie-Lynn Sigler.

The two actors have detailed their experiences with multiple sclerosis (MS), a neurological disorder that can lead to debilitating symptoms affecting daily functioning and quality of life.

Applegate, 54, has been raising awareness about the condition since her initial diagnosis in 2021.

In two podcast episodes released October 20, Applegate revealed that doctors had told her she was misdiagnosed with MS.

“She came into my room and said, ‘Congratulations, you don’t have MS,’ ” Applegate said as she fought back tears. “I was, like, not happy at all. Everybody else was so happy.”.

The “Anchorman” and “Dead to Me” actor explained that her symptoms have continued to worsen, leaving her without an explanation for what she’s experiencing as doctors investigate the cause.

Being misdiagnosed with MS is relatively common. Applegate’s revelation highlights a difficult reality for people living with unexplained symptoms resembling MS. Her experience raises questions about how MS is diagnosed, why misdiagnoses may occur, and what people can do when their symptoms don’t match their diagnosis.

In a recent development, while MS can be difficult to diagnose, an accurate diagnosis can help people with the condition gain access to appropriate treatment. A misdiagnosis, on the other hand, may lead to unnecessary interventions and medication, and take an emotional toll over time.

“MS can be challenging to diagnose because there is no single test that confirms it in every case,” said Steve Allder, MD, consultant neurologist at Re:Cognition Health.

Industry observers note that “An incorrect diagnosis can have significant consequences. Someone incorrectly diagnosed with MS may experience considerable anxiety, undergo unnecessary investigations, or receive treatments with potential risks and side effects. Equally, if MS is missed, treatment may be delayed, potentially allowing further neurological damage,” Allder told Healthline.

A 2024 systematic review and meta-analysis underscores that MS misdiagnoses remain a concern.

Research suggests that around 15% of people diagnosed with MS may actually have another condition.

However, estimates vary across studies, with some reporting rates ranging from 5–41%.

While an accurate diagnosis can guide patients toward appropriate treatment, a mistaken one may lead to unnecessary medication, emotional distress, and years of uncertainty.

Upcoming diagnostic guidelines offer hope for greater accuracy, but they also raise crucial questions about how doctors can adequately distinguish MS from other conditions.

“Research has shown that MS can be both overdiagnosed and underdiagnosed,” Allder stated.

It has been revealed that “Diagnosis relies on a combination of symptoms, neurological examination, MRI findings, and sometimes, additional tests. It is also key to recognize that diagnoses can evolve as upcoming evidence emerges. As neurologists, we must remain open to revisiting a diagnosis when symptoms or test results do not fit, ensuring patients receive appropriate treatment and support.”.

In a recent development, MS symptoms may vary widely and overlap with several other conditions. These may include:.

Because these conditions share certain features with MS, healthcare professionals should consider a patient’s full clinical profile rather than relying on a single symptom or scan.

It has been revealed that “MS can cause numbness, tingling, muscle weakness, visual disturbances, balance problems, and fatigue. However, these symptoms are not unique to the condition,” Allder noted.

In a recent development, “For example, numbness and tingling may indicate peripheral neuropathy, sometimes associated with diabetes or vitamin B12 deficiency. Weakness or altered sensation may result from a trapped nerve or spinal cord compression. Migraines can cause visual disturbances and sensory symptoms, while inner-ear disorders may affect balance,” he continued.

Allder noted that fatigue is particularly nonspecific and may be associated with:.

He explained that, as a neurologist, he considers the pattern, duration, and progression of symptoms alongside examination findings.

“No single symptom automatically indicates MS. A thorough assessment is essential to identify the underlying cause and ensure the patient receives appropriate treatment,” he said.

There is no single test that definitively confirms every case of MS.

Diagnosis typically involves reviewing symptoms, conducting neurological examinations, and evaluating MRI scans and laboratory results.

MRI findings may be tricky to interpret. Some white-matter spots resemble MS lesions but may result from migraine, aging, or other conditions. Misapplying diagnostic criteria or overlooking alternative explanations can also lead to mistakes.

Sources indicate that “MRI abnormalities alone do not confirm MS,” Allder noted. “The diagnosis must be based on the overall clinical picture, with alternative explanations carefully considered.”.

Research also suggests that MS misdiagnosis rates may differ by sex.

Research reveals females are 2.1 times more likely to be misdiagnosed with MS than males, highlighting the potential for diagnostic bias and differences in how symptoms are evaluated.

The updated MS diagnostic criteria published in 2025 offer a framework for improving diagnosis.

The updated guidelines introduce several vital changes.

For instance, the optic nerve (the nerve connecting the eye to the brain) is now included as a fifth anatomical location for assessing evidence of MS.

The revised criteria also include fresh MRI biomarkers, such as the central vein sign and paramagnetic rim lesions. These features can help doctors distinguish MS-related abnormalities from other conditions.

These changes may help doctors diagnose MS earlier and more accurately.

Industry observers note that if you experience persistent or recurring neurological symptoms, seek medical advice. Your doctor can assess your symptoms and, if applicable, refer you to a neurologist.

Sudden weakness, vision loss, or difficulty speaking requires urgent medical assessment, Allder remarked.

“Depending on the findings, investigations may include MRI scans of the brain and spinal cord, blood tests, and, in some cases, a lumbar puncture,” Allder noted.

“It is important that results are interpreted alongside symptoms and examination findings, as no single test should determine the diagnosis in isolation.”.

Allder remarked that if you’re unsure about a diagnosis, you can ask your neurologist what evidence supports it and whether alternative health conditions have been considered.

“A second opinion or follow-up assessment may be appropriate. The priority is an accurate diagnosis that leads to the right treatment and support,” Allder said.

Breaking: Tesla on Autopilot/FSD was going 74 mph before fiery crash that killed 3

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1144 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A Tesla Model Y left a parkway in El Dorado Hills, California, hit a tree and burst into flames in September, killing three of the four people inside.
  • It has been revealed that the crash was widely covered in the Sacramento area as a fiery single-car wreck.
  • Sources indicate that late on Saturday, September 12, 2026, a 2024 Tesla Model Y with four people inside was heading west on Serrano Parkway, between Terracina Drive and Silva Valley Parkway.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A Tesla Model Y left a parkway in El Dorado Hills, California, hit a tree and burst into flames in September, killing three of the four people inside. Tesla’s own report to federal regulators indicates Autopilot or “Full Self-Driving” was engaged, with the car doing 74 mph.

It has been revealed that the crash was widely covered in the Sacramento area as a fiery single-car wreck. None of that coverage mentioned a driver-assist system. It’s the latest case in our ongoing investigation into fatal crashes hidden in Tesla’s NHTSA data.

Sources indicate that late on Saturday, September 12, 2026, a 2024 Tesla Model Y with four people inside was heading west on Serrano Parkway, between Terracina Drive and Silva Valley Parkway. That’s a residential part of the Serrano community in El Dorado Hills, east of Sacramento.

According to the CHP’s Placerville office, the Model Y left the road “for unknown reasons,” hit a tree on the north side of the parkway, and caught fire. Officers got the call around 10:38 p.m. By the time they arrived, the car was fully engulfed in flames.

Charles Anthony Cameron, 30, of Sacramento, was thrown from the car and died at the scene. Alejandra Mendoza, 28, of Sacramento, and Kailauna Viola Mills, 28, of Roseville, were found dead inside once firefighters put out the fire. One of the two women was driving; CHP hasn’t publicly said which.

Recent findings suggest that mills lived in Arizona and was visiting family. Her uncle told CBS Sacramento she worked in the medical field and was supposed to get married next April.

A fourth person, a 28-year-old Sacramento woman, survived with major injuries.

It has been revealed that CHP says the cause is still under investigation. Speed, impairment, and how the car left the road haven’t been released. And nobody has said a word about Autopilot.

Under NHTSA’s Standing General Order, automakers have to report crashes where a Level 2 driver-assist system was engaged within 30 seconds of impact and someone is killed or hurt. Tesla filed a report on this one.

It lists a 2024 Model Y, a consumer vehicle, and marks the “Engagement Status” as “Verified Engaged.” That’s Tesla confirming through its own telematics that Autopilot or FSD was on. It logs a pre-crash speed of 74 mph, a fatality, and the California Highway Patrol as the investigating agency.

Then it redacts the narrative, the software version, and whether the road was inside the system’s operating domain, all as “confidential business information,” the same treatment Tesla gives 99.9% of its reports.

The rest of the report is strangely thin. Tesla lists the roadway type as “Unknown” and what the car hit as “Unknown,” even though police noted it was a tree. It checks only one source for how it learned of the crash: the media. So Tesla found out about a triple-fatal crash in one of its cars from the news, then went into its own data and confirmed its driver-assist was on.

It has been revealed that how we matched it: Tesla logged the incident time as 05:36 UTC, which is 10:36 p.m. Pacific on September 12, within two minutes of the 10:38 p.m. call CHP responded to. The city, the 2024 Model Y, the month, and the fatal outcome all line up. It’s the only fatal Tesla driver-assist report from El Dorado Hills in the data. It’s the same crash.

Sources indicate that two of the three victims were found inside the car after the fire was out. The survivor got out of, or was pulled from, the wreckage, depending on the report.

According to recent reports, CHP hasn’t said whether the doors played any role, and we’re not suggesting they did. But it’s a fair question to ask about any Tesla crash with a fire, now that NHTSA is writing new rules for emergency door releases after years of complaints about people getting trapped. We’ve asked.

This is the second triple-fatal crash in Tesla’s latest NHTSA filings where its driver-assist was verified engaged and the public never heard about it. The other one was on I-75 in Naples. Add Vineland and July’s four fatal crashes, and the pattern is hard to miss.

"what little effort went into the report"?

I disagree, a lot of effort went in to minimize the report, to portray it as an unremarkable accident.

That is the effort I find Tesla criminally responsible for.

According to recent reports, the CHP need the full report, no redactions. If they chose to censor it that is their task, not Tesla's.

According to recent reports, what stands out in this one is how little effort went into the report. Tesla knows the speed, knows the system was on, and has telematics. But it couldn’t fill in what the car hit, and it learned about three deaths in one of its cars from the news. Then it redacted the one field, the narrative, that would tell us what the car did.

According to recent reports, tesla wants regulators and customers to trust FSD with no one watching. That trust has to be earned with data. A company that seals the account of what its car did at 74 mph in a neighborhood, in a crash that killed three people, isn’t earning it.

We’re asking CHP Placerville whether its investigators knew the system was engaged, whether they got Tesla’s raw data or Tesla’s summary of it, and what they found about the fire and the doors. If CHP never got the full data, how will it ever determine the cause?

The Part of Your Holiday Hangover You Can’t See

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (634 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Your liver probably would have liked for you to stop at the third scoop, but you’re in this together.
  • Recent findings suggest that the liver is a workhorse that plays a role in over 500 bodily functions, which include filtering toxins, regulating blood sugar, processing cholesterol, and more.
  • WHEN YOU HAVE a drink or two, your liver kicks into gear and performs triage: It transforms alcohol into harmless water and carbon dioxide, which you then pee out or exhale.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

FOUR GLASSES OF wine? Your liver drinks them, too. Extra gravy? Your liver probably would have liked for you to stop at the third scoop, but you’re in this together. Nearly every bite you eat and every drink you down ends up getting managed by the same organ in your body: your liver.

Recent findings suggest that the liver is a workhorse that plays a role in over 500 bodily functions, which include filtering toxins, regulating blood sugar, processing cholesterol, and more. But come the holidays, all the food and festive drinking can put your body’s largest organ to the test. Here’s how the wreckage happens and how to avoid accumulating long-term damage.

WHEN YOU HAVE a drink or two, your liver kicks into gear and performs triage: It transforms alcohol into harmless water and carbon dioxide, which you then pee out or exhale. The liver also holds on to anything it can use, such as the antioxidants in wine or the carbs in beer. But that doesn’t mean alcohol is nutritious. Metabolizing alcohol also creates fatty acids along the way, which get stored as triglycerides—a kind of cholesterol—until your body can use them up. Typically, if you eat and drink moderately, your body processes them just fine. Until you...

THE MORE YOU drink, the more your liver shuffles those triglycerides into the “burn later” pile...until the pile is so significant that your liver can’t get to the bottom of it.

“If you binge, then binge again, then binge again, your liver gets shocked each time and can’t recover,” says Christopher Koh, MD, clinical director at the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases.

You may not feel the damage on your liver after the holiday or the next one. But over time, the holidays may overwhelm the organ. This can look like increased inflammation that eventually kills off liver cells, leaving scar tissue in their place (and can lead to cirrhosis, a problem in which 25- to 34-year-olds have the highest risk of death compared with other age groups). Not good. Experts say just three get-togethers a week through the holiday season can initiate inflammation if each outing involves more than five servings of alcohol in two hours. Not to mention when...

YOU DON’T EVEN have to drink alcohol to mess up your liver. Seasonal foods (you know the sides that are delicious but are high in saturated fat or refined carbs, along with processed red meat) combined with holiday-associated weight gain may increase the risk of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), formerly known as nonalcoholic fatty liver disease.

“It’s estimated that up to 30 percent of the US population has [MASLD], and there aren’t symptoms, so people usually don’t know and aren’t doing anything to reverse it,” says Mazen Noureddin, MD, hepatologist at Houston Methodist.

Sources indicate that as obesity continues to rise, researchers estimate MASLD rates will rise to over 41 percent of the US population in 2050. That fat is wreaking the same havoc alcohol does—causing inflammation and eventual scarring—without the libations. MASLD may develop in as little as six weeks if you really overdo it.

Recent findings suggest that YOU DON’T NEED to buy an activated-charcoal smoothie or a beet-juice detox cleanse to do it. Your liver can regenerate and naturally get itself back in working order if you move the heck out of its way. A month or so without a drop of alcohol (no beer during the game, no wine during date night) can reduce the fat storage in the liver and help tame inflammation. You can also undo some of the fat that causes MASLD by cleaning up your diet and cutting portion sizes: Losing 5 percent of your weight can reduce up to 25 percent of liver fat.

Samsung Frame Pro TV Review, Tested by AD (2026)

📅 20 Nov 2025 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1407 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Architecturaldigest

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A staple in most modern homes, televisions often war against the ongoing aesthetics of a space in their off-time.
  • Eagle eyes will have spotted the Frame across many of our home tours—including some celebrity abodes, like the living room of Jesse Tyler Ferguson’s Fresh York pied-a-terre.
  • It has been revealed that as a design devotee and AD’s resident television and film-obsessive, I tried out the Frame Pro to see if it really measured up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A staple in most modern homes, televisions often war against the ongoing aesthetics of a space in their off-time. Masquerading as artwork, the Samsung Frame TV offers an alternative in the world of home entertainment that amplifies interior design instead of taking away from it.

Eagle eyes will have spotted the Frame across many of our home tours—including some celebrity abodes, like the living room of Jesse Tyler Ferguson’s Fresh York pied-a-terre. With their art-forward ideology, it’s clear to see why the Frame line is favored by designers. After all, a big black screen is not really enhancing the visual impact of a living room.

It has been revealed that as a design devotee and AD’s resident television and film-obsessive, I tried out the Frame Pro to see if it really measured up. Boasting the same matte finish display as the original model but with brighter picture quality, fully wireless outputs, and a bevy of technical upgrades, the Frame Pro has features to offer for tech purists and design-heads alike.

How much does it cost? Are there payment plans available?

The Frame Pro starts at $2,200—though is already marked down for Black Friday, and may drop further in price closer to the shopping holiday. Payment intends are available through Affirm, with options up to four installments, the lowest being $400 every two weeks.

What are the customization options?

The Frame Pro comes in three sizes, starting at 65 inches and going up in ten inch intervals to 85 inches. I opted for the smallest size to best fit my available wall space, and chose a white bezel border (brown and teak are the other colorways) to coordinate with the frames on the wall art in my living room.

What was the delivery process like?

A service coordinated the delivery window with me over email and helped to set up the television once they arrived to make sure it was functioning properly. Despite what the name would have you believe, the Frame Pro does, in fact, have attachable legs. The delivery service did not include mounting, so the team merely helped lift the Frame Pro onto my TV stand and set it up in a freestanding format.

In a recent development, what was the installation process like? How long did it take, and how many people?

The Frame Pro has a very slim mounting system consisting of two brackets. The installation kit comes with a paper template with the layout of the brackets printed on it. The process was fairly straightforward, though I wish the step-by-step manual had more text included rather than just showing images of the process.

Recent findings suggest that although the brackets have several slots to accommodate differing stud widths, we ran into an concern where the distance between the studs in our building didn’t quite align with the bracket slots to center it on the wall while also keeping the TV secure in the studs. In the end, we ended up hanging the TV ever so slightly off-center in order to keep the screws aligned with the studs. For peace of mind, we added drywall anchors and screws to the center-most slots of the bracket for some additional support to help distribute the weight a bit more.

Recent findings suggest that hanging the TV from the bracket was simple, and because the screw-in panels on the back are magnetized, it made it feel more secure when we slotted it into place. At just under 50 pounds, the TV wasn’t all that heavy, though because of the larger size, we did need two people (and another to guide the way) to lift it in place. The bezel is also magnetized, so the four pieces simply snap onto the exterior of the TV once you have it hung up.

Overall, the mounting process took us about two hours to complete but I think it could likely be decreased down to one hour (and possibly even less) had it not been for our particular concerns with the stud distances that needed a lot of remeasuring and even a last-minute trip to the hardware store for a stud finder.

Industry observers note that as the Frame’s main draw, I was most eager to see art mode in action. The artwork is selected either through Samsung’s Art Store (which requires a $4.99 per month subscription) or through personally uploaded photos to the SmartThings companion app. To really be convincing as artwork, the photos need to be high quality—you wouldn’t notice any blurriness when seeing the Mona Lisa at the Louvre, would you? For older artworks, I was able to find plenty of high resolution files available for free through museum or crowdsourced websites. Once you make sure its resolution matches the 4K sizing of the Frame (3,840 x 2,160 pixels), you simply upload the image and select if you want a matboard added to the border. If you upload a smaller size image, you can expect to see some amount of graininess once it loads on the screen. I chose a selection of paintings by Vincent Van Gogh, Georgia O’Keefe, and Claude Monet, among other artists with the rotating gallery feature. While essentially all the artwork I tested out looked beautiful on the screen, the paintings with thicker brushstrokes made me want to reach out and touch it to see if it was real.

I found that the art mode is most convincing when you’re in a well-lit room. Even though the TV brightness does adjust automatically—and has motion sensors so it only turns on when someone enters a room if you want to leave it on all day—the fact that it’s a screen becomes more obvious in low-light environments. Even at its lowest brightness setting, when in art mode in a dark room, the screen slightly illuminates the space, no longer tricking your eyes that it’s artwork.

It has been revealed that in terms of the viewing experience, the Frame Pro certainly leveled up my weekly binge watches. The image is incredibly crisp, and when rewatching highlights I’d seen before (I’m a creature of habit, what can I say), I noticed the colors were markedly more vivid than on my previous TV. The Neo QLED panel, a.k.a. mini LEDs, makes a massive difference in the contrast of colors on the TV, and it’s all the more enjoyable to see ingenious set designs from my favorite shows and movies.

One of the substantial differences between the Frame Pro and previous models is the Wireless One Connect box. Where the regular Frame model has a slim transparent cord connected to the box that contains HDMI and other outputs, the Frame Pro is fully wireless, meaning the only cable coming out of the TV is the power cord. I have fairly speedy and reliable internet so there haven’t been any problems with connection being wireless. Plus, I love the clean look the lack of cords provides. The only time I noticed lag was when I tried using Chromecast from my phone to try and stream content. It took longer to load and had some clarity issues in the picture. That’s not true for everything I cast, as a movie I mirrored through AirPlay loaded easily, so I think it might have been due to an incompatibility with Google’s casting software or the phone it was being routed through.

I’ve had the Frame Pro for over a year now and haven’t noticed any difference in visual quality or functionality when watching different indicates or movies. Style-wise, I’ve loved decorating around the Frame as the seasons change. The minimalist white base doesn’t detract from surrounding decor, like pumpkins during Halloween and garland and ornaments around Christmas. I’ve subbed in a few different pieces of artwork in the art library, particularly during hosting season when I want to curate a cozier vibe with an autumnal artwork or yule log video. The automatic software updates keep the TV functioning at a high level, even as streaming apps regularly change.

It’s safe to say that I’m keeping this TV for as long as possible. Even as someone who loves to watch shows and movies, I don’t want the entire design of my living room to revolve around a television. The slim design of the Frame really shifts the focus to the other furniture and decor in the space, and makes my space feel more centered around the memories made inside it.

RFK Jr.’s Revised Vaccine Schedule May Cause 83% Surge in Hepatitis B Infections

📅 21 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1001 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F.
  • Concerns include a rise in preventable infectious diseases such as measles, polio, and hepatitis B.
  • A new study suggests that delaying or foregoing the hepatitis B shot for newborns could increase chronic infections among children.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s proposed changes to the childhood vaccine schedule have raised alarm among public health experts and researchers.

Concerns include a rise in preventable infectious diseases such as measles, polio, and hepatitis B.

A new study suggests that delaying or foregoing the hepatitis B shot for newborns could increase chronic infections among children.

In December 2025, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) ended its recommendation for universal hepatitis B vaccination at birth for infants whose mothers test negative for the virus. Instead, the federal health agency recommends individual-based clinical decision making.

After reviewing the evidence, the CDC, which is overseen by the HHS, concluded that newborns “face little risk of contracting hepatitis,” which deemed the vaccine, typically administered at birth, unnecessary.

Experts say this shift in public health policy wasn’t based on science, and researchers warn of rising infection rates.

“Hepatitis B immunizations have been proven to protect individuals against a serious and significant disease,” mentioned Graham Tse, MD, pediatrician and chief medical officer of MemorialCare Miller Children’s & Women’s Hospital in Long Beach, CA.

“The hepatitis B vaccines have several decades of history and have been proven safe and effective,” Tse said. “There has been no upcoming data or evidence presented or uncovered to support delaying the newborn dose of hepatitis B.”.

Here’s what parents should know about making informed decisions with their child’s healthcare team.

In a recent development, A U.S. modeling study published in Annals of Internal Medicine on October 20 projected that delaying the first vaccine dose until 2 months could increase chronic hepatitis B infections among infants by 19% under one scenario.

With shared decision making and lower vaccine uptake, projected increases ranged from 83% to 225%, compared with universal birth-dose vaccination.

The researchers also estimated that up to 1.8 million young adults could remain susceptible to hepatitis B by age 20 under shared decision making, compared with 232,000 under universal birth dosing.

Another study published in JAMA Pediatrics in late April projected hundreds of additional chronic infections annually if the hepatitis B birth dose were delayed or omitted.

However, these figures are model-based projections, rather than verified outcomes. Actual results will depend on vaccination rates and other factors.

In December 2025, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) adopted a recommendation shifting away from universal hepatitis B vaccination at birth for infants whose mothers test negative for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg).

Under the new approach, parents and healthcare professionals can decide together whether to give the first dose at birth or defer it until the baby is 2 months old.

Sources indicate that the change followed an 8 to 3 vote by the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP), marking a departure from longstanding U.S. guidance.

However, infants born to mothers who test positive for hepatitis B or whose infection status is unknown should still receive the hepatitis B vaccine and hepatitis B immune globulin (HBIG) within 12 hours of birth, according to the updated guidelines.

Hepatitis B is a viral infection that affects the liver.

Although some infections resolve, newborns and infants face a higher risk of developing lifelong hepatitis B infection compared with adults.

Up to 90% of infants infected during their first year develop chronic hepatitis B.

“We have actual world evidence that vaccinating newborns for hepatitis B prevents hepatitis B infections later in life and the serious complications of that disease,” Tse mentioned.

Over time, chronic infection can lead to cirrhosis, liver failure, or liver cancer.

“The danger of delaying the newborn hepatitis B shot is that individuals do not get vaccinated and thereby do not have protection against hepatitis B,” Tse remarked.

Early vaccination helps protect young infants before potential exposure occurs, including situations in which maternal screening misses an infection.

“Newborns can be infected with hepatitis B from a mother who is not aware they have a hepatitis B infection or from exposure later in life,” Tse said.

“The risk is developing a hepatitis B infection, which can potentially lead to liver cancer, fulminant hepatitis, or severe end-stage liver disease.”.

In contrast to the CDC, the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) still recommends a universal hepatitis B vaccine dose within 24 hours of birth, followed by additional doses during infancy.

The leading pediatric medical organization has raised concerns about the potential consequences of reduced vaccination rates.

The hepatitis B vaccine has decades of safety and effectiveness data.

Tse remarked the AAP’s vaccine schedule and recommendations are based on decades of study, use, and expert input, and provide the best protection against vaccine-preventable diseases.

Parents who have questions about potential side effects, timing, or their baby’s individual risk should discuss them with a qualified healthcare professional.

“Parents are confused, given the recommendations from CDC, HHS, and Kennedy differ from established and respected groups such as the American Academy of Pediatrics, the Infectious Disease Society of America, and several states,” Tse noted.

“Parents desire to keep their children safe, and having differing opinions and confusion will lead to reduced vaccination rates as parents experience doubt as to whom to listen to or believe.”.

While the updated CDC policy offers more flexibility for some families, lower vaccination uptake could lead to an increase in chronic hepatitis B infections.

Ask your pediatrician about the benefits of vaccination against hepatitis B at birth, the risks of delaying the first dose, and the recommended schedule for completing the series.

You can also ask how maternal screening results affect your baby’s protection.

An informed conversation with your healthcare professional can help you weigh the evidence and choose a vaccination plan for your baby.

“I see no argument whatsoever for changing the established vaccination schedule for hepatitis B,” Tse mentioned.

“There have been no newly introduced studies, no data, nor evidence to justify Kennedy’s proposed changes to the childhood immunization schedule. Delaying vaccinations or skipping vaccinations puts your child at risk for serious and significant diseases, which are all preventable,” Tse stated.

#168686. Why Sleep Consistency May Be the Missing Piece When It Comes to Heart Health
